text.en:
In Maya's class the teacher once chose the monitor herself. Next term she asked all the children to vote, and a new monitor was picked.
"This time I feel it is my choice too," said Maya.

In a monarchy a king or queen rules and the position usually passes to the next member of the royal family. In ancient India there were also assemblies and councils that advised some rulers.
In a democracy the people choose their rulers by voting in elections. Every adult citizen has one vote, regardless of religion, caste, gender or wealth. India is the world's largest democracy.
Democratic governments are answerable to people, who can criticise and change them. A good democracy needs free elections, equal rights, the rule of law and citizens who take part.
In a monarchy a king or queen rules, and the title usually passes within the family.
In a democracy the people choose their rulers by voting.
Every adult citizen has one vote.
A democratic government is answerable to the people.

problem.en: How is choosing a ruler in a democracy different from a monarchy?

text.en: In a monarchy the ruler is usually born into the royal family.
In a democracy people vote to choose the ruler.
So in a democracy the people hold power.

why.en: Rulers can be changed by elections.

prompt.en: A friend says voting is not important because one vote does not matter. How will you reply?

requiredIdeas.en: Many votes together decide who governs.
If everyone thought so, nobody would vote.

points.en: Monarchy: rule by a king or queen.
Democracy: rule by representatives chosen by the people.
India is the world's largest democracy.
